big_case_rationale: Technical federal habeas appellate procedure question under 28 U.S.C. 2253(c) resolving a 6-2 circuit split over whether binding circuit precedent categorically bars a certificate of appealability when another circuit disagrees; significant for federal post-conviction and en banc practice in the Fifth and Eleventh Circuits, though modest in broader public salience.

semantic_claims.proposition: The Court holds that under the text of 28 U.S.C. 2253(c)(2) and Miller-El v. Cockrell, 537 U.S. 322, 338 (2003), a constitutional claim is debatable among jurists of reason when another federal court of appeals has resolved the issue in the applicant's favor, even if binding circuit precedent forecloses relief before a three-judge panel of the court of appeals.

The Court announces a general rule rejecting categorical circuit-precedent bars to a certificate of appealability under 28 U.S.C. 2253(c), while vacating and remanding without deciding whether petitioner's underlying 18 U.S.C. 924(c) attempted-carjacking claim is otherwise barred by the elements clause or procedural default.
